clue.text: Go back inside — downright presumptuous!

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece is placed within the other word

parts.note: arrant means downright, out-and-out

indicators.note: back tells us the little word go is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone who goes back in with downright cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone arrogantly overconfident and haughty in manner.

clue.text: It is under a pound — expensive at first sight though

indicators.note: in a down answer, being under means coming after the earlier pieces

parts.note: LB is the abbreviation for a pound weight

indicators.note: what is seen first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something costing under a pound looks pricey at first glance, though.
explanation.definitionFit: Albeit is a conjunction meaning even though or although.

clue.text: Soldiers listen to girl's recital

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to hear is to listen
Sal is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Troops are made to hear a girl's musical performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice performance, a run-through of a piece.

clue.text: Well-bred fellow — an evasive person

parts.note: a gent is a fellow, a man
a slippery, evasive person is called an eel

explanation.surface: A refined man turns out to be slippery.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means refined and polite, with upper-class manners.

clue.text: Crazy letter from abroad ends in doubt about insanity

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: ends in points to the last letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A foreign letter raises doubts about someone's sanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutty is slang for mad, as in nuts.

clue.text: Walked leisurely behind a doctor

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree, so a doctor
to walk behind someone is to be led by them

explanation.surface: Someone strolls along in the wake of a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces in answer order: A MB LED, 'a doctor led', which is what happens when you walk behind one.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to stroll at an easy, unhurried pace.

clue.text: First Scot on the road?

parts.note: the first man, Adam, given a Scottish Mac prefix, gives a road surface named after the Scottish engineer John McAdam

explanation.surface: Asking which Scotsman set out first on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: John McAdam was a Scottish engineer whose crushed-stone road surface bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Macadam is a road surface of compacted broken stone.

clue.text: Enrol in movement one who avoids others

indicators.note: in movement says the letters are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Join a political movement, says someone who shuns company.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person who keeps away from company is a loner.

clue.text: Find out about messy divorces

indicators.note: messy suggests the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone learns the details of acrimonious marital breakups.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to learn or find something out.

clue.text: Leave occupied premises, covered by genuine compensation

indicators.note: covered by says one word is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: real means genuine
to quit is to vacate a place you occupied

explanation.surface: Tenants who vacate are given real compensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Requital is repayment or recompense for something given or suffered.

clue.text: Backing the prospects not obvious to the public

parts.note: backing a cause is being behind it
prospects are views, outlooks, scenes

explanation.surface: Supporting the outlook for something that the public cannot see.
explanation.definitionFit: Things done out of public view happen offstage, away from the audience.

clue.text: Descriptive language in publication that is outside the limits of respectability

indicators.note: outside says the abbreviation for that is wraps around the publication

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a mag, short for magazine, is a publication

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Colourful prose in a magazine that goes beyond decency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'publication' and 'that is' make the word IMAGE before the outer letters of 'respectability' are added.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is vivid figurative wording that paints pictures for a reader.

clue.text: Upset about some work experience

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to upset plans is to undo them
an erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Distress over a bit of work experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the definition of a distressed person, but it is the verb meaning to undo.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to go through or experience it.

clue.text: Job comes before his poetry

parts.note: in the Bible the Book of Job is followed by the Book of Psalms, whose author wrote that poetry

explanation.surface: A poet is told his job must take priority over his verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like employment but is the biblical book, which precedes Psalms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Psalms are sacred songs attributed to David, writer of that poetic book.

clue.text: Unexpected gain is in the stars, perhaps

indicators.note: unexpected suggests the letters land in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A windfall is written in the stars, like astrology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests astrology, but stars worn on a uniform are badges of rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Badges of rank or office, such as stars on an officer's shoulder, are examples.

clue.text: Poor observer in army operational sector

indicators.note: sector says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A short-sighted lookout posted in a military zone of operations.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sighted person sees distant things badly, a weak watcher.

clue.text: Sharp-eyed old black man

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a man can mean a manservant

explanation.surface: An old black man described as having keen eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant means quick to notice things.

clue.text: Ancient Jewish sectarian hothead occupying capital quarters

indicators.note: occupying says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Paris is the French capital
the head of the word hot is its first letter
E (east) is a compass quarter, so two quarters are E and E

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered zealot of old moves into lodgings in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hothead' looks like a firebrand; it is H, the head of 'hot', put into PARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees were a strict Jewish sect of the Second Temple era.

clue.text: Outlets from sinks

definitions.meaning: in golf, to sink a putt is to hole it

explanation.surface: Drainage points coming from kitchen basins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinks' looks like basins but is a verb from golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaps let things out, and a golfer who putts the ball in has holed it.

clue.text: Man of intelligence accommodates perhaps nine in brake

indicators.note: accommodates means takes in, so one piece is placed inside

parts.note: a spy works in intelligence

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word may be rearranged

explanation.surface: An agent squeezes nine people into a large carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brake' looks like a car part or an old carriage but here means a thicket.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake is a thicket, and a spinney is a small wood or copse.

clue.text: One at the start of courtship is married — what a faux pas!

parts.note: sole means one and only

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone already married begins courting a new partner, a social blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a breach of etiquette or grammar, a social blunder.

clue.text: Two fellows who translated epics

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A pair of men who rendered great epic poems into English.
explanation.walkthrough: George Chapman's Elizabethan translation of Homer inspired Keats's famous sonnet.
explanation.definitionFit: George Chapman translated Homer's Iliad and Odyssey into English verse.

clue.text: Offer to ride bicycle, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken and we write a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to pedal is to ride a bicycle

explanation.surface: A proposal to go cycling.
explanation.definitionFit: To peddle goods is to hawk or offer them for sale.

clue.text: Legendary bird monarch, dancing

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird from the Arabian Nights
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A mythical bird and a king are seen dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock is to dance to rock-and-roll music.

clue.text: Ring accountants at the top of the tree

indicators.note: in a down answer the pieces at the top come before the final letter

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
a second chartered accountant, CA
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Phone the accountants who sit at the top of the hierarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacao is the tropical tree whose beans give cocoa and chocolate.

clue.text: I repair broken-down schooner, perhaps

indicators.note: broken-down suggests the letters are smashed and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone vows to fix a dilapidated sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schooner' suggests a ship, but a prairie schooner was a covered wagon of the American West.
explanation.definitionFit: The covered wagon of the pioneers was called a prairie schooner, so the clue word is an example.

clue.text: Rate fixer — expert in image building

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the business of building an image
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Someone who sets fees turns out to be an expert in publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: A pacer sets the speed in a race, a pacemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who sets the speed for others in a race controls the tempo.

clue.text: Transfer in order to be next to the boss

parts.note: to second staff is to transfer them temporarily
taken as written
a command is an order

explanation.surface: An employee is moved so as to sit beside the manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy ranks just below the chief and stands in when needed.

clue.text: New York poem, reviewed in Leningrad, for example

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters are looked over again and rearranged

explanation.surface: A verse about New York gets a critical review in Soviet Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Leningrad was named after Lenin, so the city's name is a word derived from a person.

clue.text: Dark horse, possibly, holding a practice session

indicators.note: holding means one word contains the other

parts.note: a horse is an example of a brute, a beast
in cricket, nets are practice sessions in netted enclosures

explanation.surface: An unknown racehorse is having a training run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark horse' wants to be read together; 'Dark' alone is the definition. Cricket nets are practice pitches enclosed by netting.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette is a woman with dark brown hair.
